closing_postures.resolution_qualified: END by actually committing to a position: the final paragraph delivers the verdict, hedged only as much as honesty requires. Do NOT end by suspending judgment, opening a new question, or retreating into irresolution.
closing_postures.resolution_costed: END by affirming the position AND naming its concrete price in the same movement. The verdict stands; the ending is the bill, not a retreat from the verdict.
closing_postures.reframe_displace: END by relocating the real question: the closing commits to the claim that a different question or object matters more, stated as a positive finding - not as a refusal to answer.
closing_postures.refusal_suspended: The ending may leave the central tension unresolved, but the suspension must be argued as the correct verdict on the evidence - not performed as elegance or a knowing shrug.
closing_postures.refusal_dissolved: END by showing the question dissolves rather than resolves - and state plainly what the dissolution costs or licenses, so the ending is a finding, not an evasion.

items.name: The Autopsy
items.core: A debate everyone treats as settled is exhumed; the passage dissects HOW consensus formed rather than who was right; the verdict is on the process, not the question.
items.difficulty_source: separating the author's view of the debate from their view of the debate-about-the-debate

items.name: The Borrowed Lens
items.core: A framework imported from an alien discipline is applied, yields striking results, then the lens is shown to distort more than it reveals; ends on the price of borrowed vision.
items.difficulty_source: tracking when the author is USING the lens versus EXAMINING it

items.name: The Scale Shift
items.core: A claim holds at one scale (individual, local); the author zooms out and the claim inverts at the larger scale; the two scales are never reconciled.
items.difficulty_source: scope discipline — every option that ignores scale is wrong, and most readers ignore scale

items.name: The Definitional Undertow
items.core: Surface argument about a phenomenon; the real argument is about the definition of the key term, revealed when two camps are shown to be talking past each other.
items.difficulty_source: recognizing the argument is semantic without concluding it is MERELY semantic

items.name: The Reluctant Conversion
items.core: The author begins openly resistant to a position and argues themselves, step by contested step, into a version of it — while pricing what conversion cost.
items.difficulty_source: distinguishing the adopted version from the version originally resisted

items.name: The Third Thing
items.core: Two rival explanations are rehearsed and BOTH rejected for sharing a hidden premise; the passage's contribution is naming the premise, not offering a third theory.
items.difficulty_source: resisting the expectation that a third theory arrives; it never does

items.name: The Vanishing Object
items.core: Inquiry into X progressively reveals X may not be a coherent kind at all; the question is dissolved, not answered.
items.difficulty_source: the thesis is a redescription, not a position on the original question

items.name: The Costed Victory
items.core: A thesis is defended successfully; the final movement tallies what the defense had to concede; the thesis stands, diminished.
items.difficulty_source: the tone problem — triumph and loss are simultaneously true

items.name: The Time-Lag Argument
items.core: A concept is shown to be judged by criteria inherited from an era whose conditions no longer hold; the historical excavation IS the argument.
items.difficulty_source: what follows for the present is implied, never stated

items.name: The Practitioner's Rebuke
items.core: An elegant theoretical account collides with practitioner detail that breaks it; the author sides with neither and locates the value in the friction itself.
items.difficulty_source: refusing both 'theory wins' and 'practice wins' readings

items.name: The Asymmetry Hunt
items.core: Two things habitually treated as symmetric (memory/anticipation, praise/blame) are shown deeply asymmetric; consequences cascade.
items.difficulty_source: every distractor that restores symmetry is tempting and wrong

items.name: The Successful Failure
items.core: Case study of something that failed its stated goal but succeeded at an unstated one; becomes an argument about what goals are FOR.
items.difficulty_source: identifying which success the author actually credits

items.name: The Category Refugee
items.core: A phenomenon fits no existing category; each candidate category is tried and shown to mutilate it; ends on what taxonomies do to their misfits.
items.difficulty_source: the passage's positive claim is about categorization, not the phenomenon

items.name: The Inheritance Dispute
items.core: Two traditions claim the same idea or figure as ancestor; the contest over lineage reveals more than the idea itself does.
items.difficulty_source: the author's stance is on the CONTEST, not on either claimant

items.name: The Diagnostic Reversal
items.core: What is widely lamented as the disease is re-read as an adaptive response — or the celebrated cure as the pathology.
items.difficulty_source: causal-direction traps write themselves

items.name: The Silent Partner
items.core: An argument everyone makes is shown to depend on an invisible enabling condition; the passage makes it visible and asks what happens as it erodes.
items.difficulty_source: the enabling condition is stated outright, but only once, and early

items.name: The Half-Life
items.core: Traces how a concept decays as it migrates from technical origin to public discourse; asks whether the degraded version still does real work.
items.difficulty_source: the author's ambivalence — decay documented without contempt

items.name: The Double Bind
items.core: An institution faces two legitimate but incompatible demands; the passage refuses to dissolve the bind and instead maps who pays for it.
items.difficulty_source: no side is endorsed; distractors that pick a side all fail

items.name: The Wrong Question
items.core: The question as posed is patiently answered; the answer is shown unsatisfying; the question is reframed — and the new question is left unanswered.
items.difficulty_source: two-stage structure — readers freeze at the first answer

items.name: The Minority Report
items.core: A discredited or unfashionable view is steelmanned — not to endorse it, but to show what the mainstream lost by winning.
items.difficulty_source: endorsement traps — steelmanning read as advocacy

items.name: The Instrument Effect
items.core: The method of studying X is shown to partly produce the X it finds; findings about the world become findings about our instruments.
items.difficulty_source: keeping object-level and method-level claims separate

items.name: The Threshold Argument
items.core: A difference of degree becomes a difference of kind past some threshold; the entire argument is about locating — or denying the locatability of — the threshold.
items.difficulty_source: quantitative-sounding claims with qualitative stakes

items.name: The Proxy War
items.core: A minor technical dispute is anatomized as a proxy for a deep, unarguable commitment; the passage explains why proxies form where direct argument fails.
items.difficulty_source: the surface dispute is never adjudicated; readers expect adjudication

items.name: The Hospitable Critic
items.core: A body of work is reviewed with genuine admiration; a single load-bearing objection then retroactively reframes the admiration.
items.difficulty_source: tone — the admiration is sincere AND the objection is fatal

items.name: The Ecology
items.core: Agent-level explanation is refused; the phenomenon is redescribed as a system-level equilibrium; ends noting what agency-talk loses and what systems-talk cannot see.
items.difficulty_source: level-of-explanation confusions power every distractor

items.name: The Untranslatable
items.core: Organized around a concept from another language or tradition that resists translation; the resistance itself is the evidence for the thesis.
items.difficulty_source: the concept is never fully defined; options that define it are traps

items.name: The Simultaneity Problem
items.core: Two developments always narrated in causal sequence are argued to be simultaneous and mutually causing; the standard story's arrow breaks.
items.difficulty_source: temporal-order distractors — the passage denies the order every reader assumes

items.name: The Boring Truth
items.core: Spectacular explanations are rehearsed and deflated in favor of a mundane one; the sting — the mundane truth is far harder to act on.
items.difficulty_source: anticlimax as structure; readers over-read drama into the ending

items.name: The Moving Target
items.core: A critique succeeded so thoroughly that its object changed shape; is the critique now obsolete, or more necessary than ever? An argument about critique's lifecycle.
items.difficulty_source: three time-slices of the same idea must be kept apart

items.name: The Self-Application
items.core: A theory is applied to itself (expertise-skepticism voiced by an expert); the recursion is managed in the open and the passage ends inside the loop.
items.difficulty_source: the author's position is structurally unstatable; stance options must reflect that

items.name: The Load-Bearing Anecdote
items.core: Opens on a small concrete incident; each return to the anecdote extracts a different layer; the final return reverses the initial reading.
items.difficulty_source: the anecdote's function changes three times; function questions abound

items.name: The Coalition of Errors
items.core: A true conclusion is widely believed for bad reasons; the passage separates the conclusion from its popular arguments and asks whether bad reasons corrupt good beliefs.
items.difficulty_source: agreeing with the conclusion while demolishing its usual defenses

items.name: The Deepening Case
items.core: One case is examined at four increasing depths; each pass finds more than the last, and nothing the earlier passes said is withdrawn.
items.difficulty_source: no reversal to key on: the reader must track what each pass ADDS, and the thesis is the accumulated weight rather than a stated turn

items.name: The Patient Inventory
items.core: Several independent observations about one subject, set down without ranking, climax, or synthesis; their relation is left for the reader to construct.
items.difficulty_source: no hierarchy among the observations, so every which-is-most-important instinct the reader brings is unsupported by the text
items.withholds_thesis_reason: observations set down without ranking or synthesis

items.name: The Front-Loaded Thesis
items.core: The position is stated plainly in the first paragraph, then defended against three escalating objections, the last of which lands.
items.difficulty_source: the thesis is visible immediately, so difficulty lives in tracking which objection is answered, which is deflected, and which survives

items.name: The Unyielding Position
items.core: A single position argued straight through with no steelman and no concession; the opposing view is characterised only through what the argument must dispose of.
items.difficulty_source: the absence of a concession beat removes the usual foothold: a reader looking for where the author gives ground finds nothing and must key on argument structure instead

items.name: The Two Accounts
items.core: Two accounts of the same matter are developed side by side in alternating paragraphs and never reconciled; neither is refuted.
items.difficulty_source: there is no synthesis paragraph, so the reader instinct to find the author preferred account is a trap because the text supports neither
items.withholds_thesis_reason: two accounts developed in parallel and never reconciled

items.name: The Narrowing
items.core: Begins at the widest generality and narrows by stages to a single instance, ending inside that instance own detail; the general claim is never returned to.
items.difficulty_source: the thesis is located at the narrow end, so a reader who weights the opening generality, the usual habit, keys the wrong paragraph

items.name: The Widening
items.core: Starts inside one small particular and widens by stages; each widening is earned by the previous, and the final claim is the largest the particular can carry.
items.difficulty_source: each step warrant comes only from the step below it, so the reader must judge where the widening outruns its evidence

items.name: The Sequence Without Verdict
items.core: A sequence of events told in order, with no evaluative paragraph anywhere; whatever thesis exists is carried entirely by selection and emphasis.
items.difficulty_source: no paragraph states a position, so the reader must infer stance from what is included, dwelt on, and passed over quickly
items.withholds_thesis_reason: a sequence told with no evaluative paragraph anywhere
items.tier_max_reason: Scored 6.0 at elite, the lowest of any set. The judge gave family_realization 2/10: 'The passage repeatedly states evaluations' — this family's whole definition is that no paragraph states one, and the renderer would not comply. Capped at hard until the withheld-verdict instruction is enforced by the compliance auditor the way the closing register now is.

items.name: The Return
items.core: Ends on the same object it opened with, saying something that would have been unintelligible in paragraph one; nothing about the object changed, only what has been shown.
items.difficulty_source: the change is in the reader position rather than the argument, so questions about what shifted have no propositional answer in the text

items.name: The Six Witnesses
items.core: Six short paragraphs, each a different party account of one event, with no narrator adjudicating between them.
items.difficulty_source: six flat accounts and no arbitration: the reader must hold six positions at once and resist collapsing them into a majority view
items.withholds_thesis_reason: six witness accounts with no narrator adjudicating

items.name: The Long Definition
items.core: Works out what a term must mean if it is to do the job asked of it, testing candidate definitions in sequence and keeping what survives.
items.difficulty_source: the argument is analytic rather than evidential, so nothing is proved by cases and a reader hunting for evidence paragraphs misreads the structure

items.name: The Short Proof
items.core: Three paragraphs only: a claim, the one thing that would have to be true for it, and whether it is.
items.difficulty_source: compression, since with no development paragraph every sentence is load-bearing and the usual skim-for-the-turn strategy has nothing to find
items.tier_max_reason: Scored 6.8 at elite. It is the only 3-paragraph family, which at the 500-550 word band means ~180 words per paragraph against a typical ~110, and the per-paragraph cadence, word targets and trap anchoring are all tuned for 4-6. Note it also produced the only GREEN screen verdict of the session — it is the most distinctive form in the library, and it stays available at medium and hard where the paragraph budget fits.

items.name: The Question Kept Open
items.core: Each paragraph answers the previous paragraph question and raises a harder one; the last question is left standing.
items.difficulty_source: the thesis is the trajectory of the questions rather than any answer given, and every answer offered is provisional by design

items.name: The Instructions
items.core: Sets out how something is done, step by step and without evaluation, until the procedure own logic makes its cost unmistakable.
items.difficulty_source: the evaluative claim is never stated but forced by the procedure, so questions about the author position rest on inference from neutral description

items.name: The Explained Phenomenon
items.core: A phenomenon is stated plainly, its mechanism worked through, the cause behind it named, and the stakes raised — ending inside the argument rather than on a verdict.
items.difficulty_source: the mechanism has several stages and the questions turn on which stage the evidence actually reaches; a reader who takes the opening statement as the thesis keys the wrong paragraph

items.name: The Surveyed Account
items.core: An account is given, illustrated across several instances, one concession is made to a rival reading, an authority is cited, and the argument closes still in motion.
items.difficulty_source: the instances differ in what they actually establish, and the single concession is easy to mistake for the author's own position

items.name: The Defined Process
items.core: A term is fixed precisely, the process it names is worked through, instances test the definition, and the passage ends mid-argument without restating the definition.
items.difficulty_source: the definition given early does real work late, and options that use the term loosely are wrong for reasons the passage never spells out

items.name: The Traced Development
items.core: Something is dated to its origin and followed forward through how it changed, what drove each change, and why it now matters — ending inside the sequence.
items.difficulty_source: causes and consequences are adjacent in the text but not identical, and the questions separate what drove a change from what merely accompanied it

items.name: The Posed Problem
items.core: A problem is posed early, candidate explanations are worked through on their merits, and the passage settles on the one the evidence supports without ceremony.
items.difficulty_source: the rejected explanations are given real evidence too, so the reader must weigh which evidence bears on the question rather than which sounds strongest

items.name: The Asymmetry Noted
items.core: Two things treated as parallel are worked through until the parallel fails; the failure is described precisely and the passage continues from it rather than concluding.
items.difficulty_source: the asymmetry is stated once, in the middle, without emphasis — a reader tracking the surface comparison misses the sentence the whole passage turns on
